new_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Warehouse Ops Excellence
new_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

 The Material Movement & Flow (MMF) organization at Arsenal-1 is responsible for warehouse operations, inventory integrity, and material flow engineering across Anduril's multi-program defense manufacturing site. We are building a world-class operating system rooted in Toyota Production System principles, structured PDCA problem-solving, and disciplined daily management. This role is the architect of that system.

 THE ROLE 

 The Senior Manager, Warehouse Ops Excellence is the management system architect for the MMF organization. You will also serve as the operational chief of staff to the Director, Material Movement & Flow — translating strategic priorities into structured execution through the operating rhythm, decision-support packages, and organizational readiness tracking. You will design and stand up the operating rhythm, continuous improvement methodology, training infrastructure, and KPI framework that warehouse operations runs on. Once each system is established, you will coach and empower the line to maintain and evolve it independently — your success is measured by how well the systems run without you in the room.

 You will also shape the broader MMF organization as it scales — defining functional charters, role boundaries, and operating frameworks that new teams and leaders will inherit, including future inventory integrity and control leadership roles. You will architect the operating model across multiple buildings and programs as construction completes, partnering with Material Flow Engineering to ensure new spaces launch with the management system already in place.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO 

 
 Operating Rhythm: Design and facilitate the tiered daily management system — DOR, WOR, and MOR. Own templates, cadence, escalation paths, visual boards, and action tracking.

 Tier System & Leader Standard Work: Build the tier board system, leader standard work schedules, and escalation protocols. Coach supervisors and team leads on structured daily accountability.

 Toyota Kata & Continuous Improvement: Serve as the team’s Kata coach. Own the CI pipeline — Kaizen events, A3s, and savings validation.

 Production Program Accountability : Build the governance framework that defines how production programs engage with warehouse operations — SLAs for material availability, handling requirements, turnaround commitments, and regulatory compliance. Develop the scorecarding methodology and hold program leads accountable to it. Serve as the warehouse-to-planning interface alongside the MFE team.

 Training System Architecture: Design the qualification system: skills matrices, standard work documentation, onboarding programs, and train-the-trainer certification. Partner with the Warehouse Manager to build training capability within the existing team — identify and develop supervisors and team leads as certified trainers, and define the dedicated training roles the organization will need as it scales.

 KPI Design & Analytics: Define and visualize metrics across all warehouse functions using the SQDIP framework. Own the calculation methodology. Provide labor and budget analysis including headcount modeling and cost-per-unit metrics.

 Management System Audits: Design and execute layered process audits. Track standard work and leader standard work compliance. Identify systemic gaps and drive corrective actions.

 Change Management: Lead rollout of new processes, SOPs, and WMS/ERP system changes. Own communication plans, training requirements, and post-implementation verification.

 Multi-Building Operating Structure: Architect the operating model across multiple buildings and programs as the site builds out. Ensure consistency in management systems, WMS/ERP configuration, and process standards across all facilities. Partner with MFE on layout, storage strategy, and systems integration.

 Organization Design: Partner with the Director to define functional charters, role boundaries, reporting structures, and operating models for new teams and leadership positions as the organization scales.

 Director's Chief of Staff: Serve as the Director's operational chief of staff — maintain the org readiness tracker, prepare briefing packages for WOR and MOR, coordinate cross-functional priorities, and surface risks through the operating rhythm rather than ad hoc escalation. Ensure the Director's time is focused on strategic decisions by driving the structured cadence that keeps day-to-day execution on track.

 Budget Process: Own the MMF operating budget build — assemble inputs, prepare quarterly forecasts, and track actuals versus plan.

 Cross Team Collaboration:  Collaborate with cross-functional teams, which requires regular interaction with production and manufacturing stakeholders and frequently working directly on the production floor.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 7+ years in operational excellence, lean manufacturing, production system deployment, or warehouse/manufacturing operations, with 3+ years in a leadership role.

 Expertise in TPS principles: Kata coaching, A3 problem-solving, Kaizen facilitation, and standard work development.

 3+ years designing and facilitating tiered daily management systems (DOR/WOR/MOR or equivalent).

 Experience building training and qualification systems in a manufacturing or warehouse environment.

 Proficiency with KPI design, dashboards, and translating data into operational action.

 Experience with ERP/WMS platforms and managing process changes through system transitions.

 Strong analytical skills: labor modeling, budget analysis, and cost-per-unit tracking.

 Excellent communication and coaching skills across all levels — shop floor to site leadership.

 Demonstrated ability to operate as a chief of staff or right hand to a senior leader — synthesizing information, driving meeting cadence, and ensuring leadership bandwidth is protected.

 U.S. citizenship is required pursuant to contractual obligations.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, or related field.

 Defense, aerospace, or government-contract manufacturing environment experience.

 Experience scaling operations from low-volume/prototype to high-rate production.

 Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, Kata Coach certification, or equivalent credential.

 Familiarity with DFARS, ITAR, and government property requirements.

 Experience with visual management systems, layered process audits, and shop-floor information radiators.

 Track record of building management systems from scratch at a new or scaling facility.

 US Salary Range
 $143,000 — $191,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


  

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .   

  

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

new_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Mission Engineering & Operations
new_roles.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good. 

 At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

 Your Impact 

 You will lead a team of Mission Engineers who serve as Axon’s embedded builders and operational partners inside strategic public safety agencies. Mission Engineers work face-to-face with the people doing the work, diagnose how the agency operates, and build the workflows, automations, integrations, and AI-enabled solutions that measurably improve it.

 As Senior Manager, you will create the environment in which that work succeeds. You will coach experienced individual contributors, set a clear bar for technical delivery and agency partnership, and help the team turn ambiguous field problems into secure, maintainable solutions that reach production and earn sustained adoption. You will stay close enough to the portfolio to recognize patterns, anticipate risk, and connect what the team learns in the field back to Product, Engineering, and the broader organization.

 Success is reflected in agencies becoming more capable, Mission Engineers growing into trusted transformation leaders, and strong field solutions becoming reusable patterns that benefit customers beyond a single engagement. Axon’s mission is to Protect Life, and this team is one of the most direct ways we advance that mission alongside the agencies we serve.

 What You’ll Do 

 Location: Southeast US Regionally based with Travel up to 40%
 Reports to: Senior Director, Customer Deployment & Mission Engineering
 Direct Reports:   Individual Contributors

 Lead, Coach, and Develop Mission Engineers

 
 Lead and develop a distributed team of embedded Mission Engineers working across strategic agency environments

 Coach individual contributors through complex technical decisions, ambiguous customer problems, executive conversations, and high-stakes delivery moments

 Establish clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, onsite partnership, production delivery, adoption, documentation, and measurable agency impact

 Build individualized development plans and create opportunities for Mission Engineers to expand their technical range, executive presence, and transformation leadership

 Foster a culture of curiosity, candor, responsible experimentation, continuous learning, and shared accountability

 Support thoughtful team growth by selecting and onboarding people who can both build practical solutions and earn credibility with agency stakeholders

 
 Set the Bar for Agency Outcomes

 
 Ensure Mission Engineers begin with the agency’s mission, operational workflow, and desired outcome before selecting or building a solution

 Require clear baselines, success criteria, and adoption measures so impact is demonstrated rather than assumed

 Guide the team from discovery through production use, iteration, handoff, and sustained adoption

 Help Mission Engineers balance immediate agency needs with secure, maintainable, and scalable solution design

 Reinforce that success means the agency is more capable—not that one individual has become indispensable

 
 Own a Strategic Mission Engineering Portfolio

 
 Maintain visibility across strategic agencies, active builds, adoption progress, technical risk, and emerging operational needs

 Match Mission Engineer capability and level to agency complexity, transformation opportunity, and stakeholder environment

 Use operating reviews and portfolio data to identify delivery risks, recurring friction, adoption barriers, and opportunities for reuse

 Step into critical situations with structure and calm while coaching the accountable Mission Engineer to remain in ownership

 Drive consistent execution across embedded engagements without forcing every agency problem into the same playbook

 
 Advance Technical and AI-Enabled Delivery

 
 Maintain sufficient fluency across SaaS, cloud services, APIs, enterprise integrations, hardware, data, and modern AI tooling to coach technical decisions and challenge weak reasoning

 Help the team decide when to configure the platform, when to extend it, and when a net-new build is justified

 Establish expectations for validation, observability, fallback paths, maintainability, documentation, and responsible use of sensitive data

 Ensure solutions uphold CJIS requirements, evidence integrity, privacy, approved-tooling standards, and other applicable security controls

 Encourage practical use of AI to accelerate work while preserving human ownership of architecture, accuracy, and outcomes

 
 Turn Field Learning Into Organizational Leverage

 
 Build mechanisms for Mission Engineers to document and share reusable workflows, integrations, frameworks, and playbooks

 Identify patterns across agencies and help convert successful one-off solutions into repeatable capabilities

 Create strong feedback loops with Product and Engineering around recurring workflow friction, unmet operational needs, and product opportunities

 Partner with Mission Operators, Customer Success, Deployment, Professional Services, Support, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Enablement so agencies experience coordinated execution

 Share portfolio insights with senior leaders to influence investment, prioritization, staffing, and the evolution of the Mission Engineering operating model

 
 Lead Executive and Agency Engagement

 
 Build trusted relationships with command staff, agency executives, technical leaders, and internal senior leadership

 Serve as a senior partner during agency-impacting incidents, high-visibility deployments, and moments that require clear trade-offs or executive alignment

 Translate complex technical and operational issues into decisions that are clear to both technical teams and executive audiences

 Coach Mission Engineers to challenge requests constructively, communicate candidly, and leave stakeholders with a practical path forward

 
 What You Bring

 Required

 
 10+ years of experience in customer-facing technical delivery, systems integration, solutions engineering, implementation consulting, operational transformation, or comparable environments

 5+ years leading and developing senior technical individual contributors in customer-facing organizations

 Demonstrated success coaching teams that deliver secure, production-ready solutions in complex customer environments

 Experience leading distributed or field-based teams across multiple customers, regions, or engagement models

 A record of improving technical execution, adoption, operational outcomes, and delivery consistency across a portfolio

 Broad technical fluency across SaaS platforms, cloud services, APIs, networking, hardware, integrations, data workflows, and AI-enabled technologies

 Executive presence with the ability to earn trust, communicate trade-offs, and guide decisions with command staff and senior leaders

 Strong systems thinking and the ability to distinguish isolated issues from patterns that require a scalable solution

 A data-informed leadership approach using baselines, production delivery, adoption, operational improvement, quality, and reuse to evaluate performance

 Comfort leading through ambiguity while creating clarity around ownership, priorities, and success criteria

 Ability to obtain and maintain CJIS compliance and exercise sound judgment with highly sensitive information

 
 Preferred

 
 Experience in public safety, law enforcement, defense, government technology, or another mission-critical operating environment

 Familiarity with CAD, RMS, digital evidence, real-time operations, or integrated public safety ecosystems

 Experience leading teams that build automations, integrations, operational workflows, internal tools, or AI-enabled solutions

 Experience converting field-developed solutions into reusable frameworks, product improvements, or organizational playbooks

 Familiarity with technical talent development, competency frameworks, or academy-style enablement programs

 
 Additional Information

 We recognize that leaders may arrive through different paths. If you have developed technically curious customer-facing teams, helped people turn ambiguous operational problems into working solutions, and care deeply about measurable customer impact, we encourage you to apply.

 Benefits that Benefit You

 
 Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

 Discretionary paid time off

 Paid parental leave for all

 Medical, Dental, Vision plans

 Fitness Programs

 Emotional & Mental Wellness support

 Learning & Development programs

 And yes, we have snacks in our offices

 
  

 Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.
 Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

 Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Important Notes 

 The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions. 

 Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment. 

 We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at  axongreenhousesupport@axon.com  or via our  Axon Privacy Web Form . For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our  Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice. 

 Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment. 

 We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes. 

 Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers .  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com , or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com .

new_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Mission Engineering & Operations
new_roles.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good. 

 At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

 Your Impact 

 You will lead a team of Mission Engineers who serve as Axon’s embedded builders and operational partners inside strategic public safety agencies. Mission Engineers work face-to-face with the people doing the work, diagnose how the agency operates, and build the workflows, automations, integrations, and AI-enabled solutions that measurably improve it.

 As Senior Manager, you will create the environment in which that work succeeds. You will coach experienced individual contributors, set a clear bar for technical delivery and agency partnership, and help the team turn ambiguous field problems into secure, maintainable solutions that reach production and earn sustained adoption. You will stay close enough to the portfolio to recognize patterns, anticipate risk, and connect what the team learns in the field back to Product, Engineering, and the broader organization.

 Success is reflected in agencies becoming more capable, Mission Engineers growing into trusted transformation leaders, and strong field solutions becoming reusable patterns that benefit customers beyond a single engagement. Axon’s mission is to Protect Life, and this team is one of the most direct ways we advance that mission alongside the agencies we serve.

 What You’ll Do 

 Location: Southeast US Regionally based with Travel up to 40%
 Reports to: Senior Director, Customer Deployment & Mission Engineering
 Direct Reports:   Individual Contributors

 Lead, Coach, and Develop Mission Engineers

 
 Lead and develop a distributed team of embedded Mission Engineers working across strategic agency environments

 Coach individual contributors through complex technical decisions, ambiguous customer problems, executive conversations, and high-stakes delivery moments

 Establish clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, onsite partnership, production delivery, adoption, documentation, and measurable agency impact

 Build individualized development plans and create opportunities for Mission Engineers to expand their technical range, executive presence, and transformation leadership

 Foster a culture of curiosity, candor, responsible experimentation, continuous learning, and shared accountability

 Support thoughtful team growth by selecting and onboarding people who can both build practical solutions and earn credibility with agency stakeholders

 
 Set the Bar for Agency Outcomes

 
 Ensure Mission Engineers begin with the agency’s mission, operational workflow, and desired outcome before selecting or building a solution

 Require clear baselines, success criteria, and adoption measures so impact is demonstrated rather than assumed

 Guide the team from discovery through production use, iteration, handoff, and sustained adoption

 Help Mission Engineers balance immediate agency needs with secure, maintainable, and scalable solution design

 Reinforce that success means the agency is more capable—not that one individual has become indispensable

 
 Own a Strategic Mission Engineering Portfolio

 
 Maintain visibility across strategic agencies, active builds, adoption progress, technical risk, and emerging operational needs

 Match Mission Engineer capability and level to agency complexity, transformation opportunity, and stakeholder environment

 Use operating reviews and portfolio data to identify delivery risks, recurring friction, adoption barriers, and opportunities for reuse

 Step into critical situations with structure and calm while coaching the accountable Mission Engineer to remain in ownership

 Drive consistent execution across embedded engagements without forcing every agency problem into the same playbook

 
 Advance Technical and AI-Enabled Delivery

 
 Maintain sufficient fluency across SaaS, cloud services, APIs, enterprise integrations, hardware, data, and modern AI tooling to coach technical decisions and challenge weak reasoning

 Help the team decide when to configure the platform, when to extend it, and when a net-new build is justified

 Establish expectations for validation, observability, fallback paths, maintainability, documentation, and responsible use of sensitive data

 Ensure solutions uphold CJIS requirements, evidence integrity, privacy, approved-tooling standards, and other applicable security controls

 Encourage practical use of AI to accelerate work while preserving human ownership of architecture, accuracy, and outcomes

 
 Turn Field Learning Into Organizational Leverage

 
 Build mechanisms for Mission Engineers to document and share reusable workflows, integrations, frameworks, and playbooks

 Identify patterns across agencies and help convert successful one-off solutions into repeatable capabilities

 Create strong feedback loops with Product and Engineering around recurring workflow friction, unmet operational needs, and product opportunities

 Partner with Mission Operators, Customer Success, Deployment, Professional Services, Support, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Enablement so agencies experience coordinated execution

 Share portfolio insights with senior leaders to influence investment, prioritization, staffing, and the evolution of the Mission Engineering operating model

 
 Lead Executive and Agency Engagement

 
 Build trusted relationships with command staff, agency executives, technical leaders, and internal senior leadership

 Serve as a senior partner during agency-impacting incidents, high-visibility deployments, and moments that require clear trade-offs or executive alignment

 Translate complex technical and operational issues into decisions that are clear to both technical teams and executive audiences

 Coach Mission Engineers to challenge requests constructively, communicate candidly, and leave stakeholders with a practical path forward

 
 What You Bring

 Required

 
 10+ years of experience in customer-facing technical delivery, systems integration, solutions engineering, implementation consulting, operational transformation, or comparable environments

 5+ years leading and developing senior technical individual contributors in customer-facing organizations

 Demonstrated success coaching teams that deliver secure, production-ready solutions in complex customer environments

 Experience leading distributed or field-based teams across multiple customers, regions, or engagement models

 A record of improving technical execution, adoption, operational outcomes, and delivery consistency across a portfolio

 Broad technical fluency across SaaS platforms, cloud services, APIs, networking, hardware, integrations, data workflows, and AI-enabled technologies

 Executive presence with the ability to earn trust, communicate trade-offs, and guide decisions with command staff and senior leaders

 Strong systems thinking and the ability to distinguish isolated issues from patterns that require a scalable solution

 A data-informed leadership approach using baselines, production delivery, adoption, operational improvement, quality, and reuse to evaluate performance

 Comfort leading through ambiguity while creating clarity around ownership, priorities, and success criteria

 Ability to obtain and maintain CJIS compliance and exercise sound judgment with highly sensitive information

 
 Preferred

 
 Experience in public safety, law enforcement, defense, government technology, or another mission-critical operating environment

 Familiarity with CAD, RMS, digital evidence, real-time operations, or integrated public safety ecosystems

 Experience leading teams that build automations, integrations, operational workflows, internal tools, or AI-enabled solutions

 Experience converting field-developed solutions into reusable frameworks, product improvements, or organizational playbooks

 Familiarity with technical talent development, competency frameworks, or academy-style enablement programs

 
 Additional Information

 We recognize that leaders may arrive through different paths. If you have developed technically curious customer-facing teams, helped people turn ambiguous operational problems into working solutions, and care deeply about measurable customer impact, we encourage you to apply.

 Benefits that Benefit You

 
 Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

 Discretionary paid time off

 Paid parental leave for all

 Medical, Dental, Vision plans

 Fitness Programs

 Emotional & Mental Wellness support

 Learning & Development programs

 And yes, we have snacks in our offices

 
  

 Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.
 Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

 Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Important Notes 

 The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions. 

 Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment. 

 We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at  axongreenhousesupport@axon.com  or via our  Axon Privacy Web Form . For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our  Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice. 

 Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment. 

 We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes. 

 Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks. We do not make job offers via text message, WhatsApp, or instant messaging platforms without a formal interview process.  All legitimate job openings are listed on our official careers page at https://www.axon.com/careers .  If you receive a suspicious offer or outreach from an email address that is not @axon.com , or if you are asked for sensitive personal information (bank details, Social Security Number) prematurely, please ignore the message and report it to recruitingops@axon.com .

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality (Floor Leader)
new_roles.description:
At GE Appliances, a Haier company, we come together to make “good things, for life.”  As the fastest-growing appliance company in the U.S., we’re powered by creators, thinkers and makers who believe that anything is possible and that there’s always a better way.  We believe in the power of our people and in giving them the freedom to explore, discover and build good things, together.  

 The GE Appliances philosophy, backed by three simple commitments defines the way we work, invent, create, do business, and serve our communities:  we come together ,  we always look for a better way , and  we create possibilities . 

 Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and must be able to maintain such authorization without current or future employer or school sponsorship. GE Appliances will not sponsor employment-based visas for this position now or in the future.

 Interested in joining us on our journey? 

he Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for plant quality performance, compliance, and continuous improvement within a high-volume manufacturing environment. This role leads the Quality Floor team and oversees production quality, component testing, Manufacturing Control Plan (MCP) auditing, and quality improvement initiatives to ensure products and processes consistently meet established standards.

Partnering closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supplier Quality, and other cross-functional teams, this leader drives structured problem-solving, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive actions to reduce defects, minimize scrap and rework, and improve process capability. The Senior Manager establishes a proactive quality culture by strengthening process controls, reinforcing standard work, and using data-driven insights to identify risks and prevent recurring issues. Through strong team leadership and a focus on sustainable results, this role helps improve product reliability, reduce the cost of poor quality, and strengthen manufacturing performance. 
 Position 
Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality (Floor Leader) 
 Location 
USA, Decatur, AL 
 
 How You'll Create Possibilities 
 Live, promote and support the Appliance Production System (APS) philosophy and drive continuous improvement in the quality and adjacent areas.  Coach all team members to ensure cross-functional, focused collaboration is the way we work. 
 Partner with the Product Line Quality, Business Operations and Manufacturing Engineering Leaders to promote a culture that establishes, sustains and improves product quality through engineering problem solving and discipline around supporting systems.  Promote a method-based quick response to new issues. 
 Responsible for developing team performance metrics tied to the overall factory (FPY, EOLA, Scrap) and product line financial plan (Warranty, Damage, Concessions, Scrap, Consumer Education).  Leads team to identify and complete projects and tasks supporting this effort.  Owns and assigns tasks and establishes accountability at the appropriate level.    
 Closely collaborates with the product line Engineering, Field Quality and Service organizations to understand and respond to part or system product level performance issues impacting owner use and satisfaction. Responds to this data in addition to internal data streams (leading indicators) for product quality and reliability (Engineering, EOLA and CAT / CUT labs).   
 Identify and execute projects to improve the costing of operations, broad owner for Corrective and Preventative Actions (CAPA), Corrective Action Request (CAR) approach to problem solving. 
 Work with Design, Operations and Quality Leadership to prioritize funding/resources to meet targets, support Continuous Improvement. 
 Owner of all attributes of the Manufacturing Control Plan for broad areas.  Responsible for the training, execution, auditing and improvement of the Manufacturing Quality Control Plan.  Support efforts intended to improve work station documentation process; create, update and maintain Manufacturing Control Instructions (MCI’s), visual aid and alerts (single point lessons) as needed. 
 Provide technical oversight to drive the development, sustainment and continuous improvement of factory quality. 
 
 
 What You'll Bring to Our Team 
 Bachelor of Science Degree in Engineering or related discipline
 7+ years of experience with manufacturing quality/NPI quality projects and process improvement
 Experience with product and process Quality Management System development and implementation
 Previous team and project leadership, including demonstration of goal setting, monitoring of performance v goals and a strong feedback / development / accountability cycle 
 Must be skilled in Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Minitab and Outlook.
 
 Working Conditions: 
 Working conditions are normal for a high-volume manufacturing environment.
 Working in this environment requires the use of safety equipment to include but not limited to; eye safety glasses, hearing protectors, work boots, and hard hats.
 These roles require frequent walking in a manufacturing plant environment.
 Hours & Weekends: Working off-shift and weekends may be required.
 
 
 Our Culture 
 Our work is centered on our People and Culture as reflected in our Zero Distance philosophy and we recognize the importance of reaffirming our commitment to inclusion and diversity (I&D). This underscores our commitment to fostering an environment where every individual feels valued, connected, and empowered to contribute, while positioning our organization to adapt seamlessly to the evolving needs of our workforce and communities. 

 This reflects our dedication to creating solutions that: Empower colleagues by fostering an environment where all voices are heard, valued, and encouraged to contribute. Strengthen communities where we live and work. Reinforce a culture of belonging, purpose, and engagement. Reflect the diversity of the communities we serve through our workforce, products, and practices. 

 By further embedding Zero Distance into our People and Culture framework, we will continue to build a deeply connected organization. We are cultivating a culture of engagement, belonging, and connection, because while attracting new talent remains a priority, retention is a cornerstone of our strategy. 
 
 
 
 GE Appliances is a trust-based organization. It is important we offer our employees the flexibility they need to do their best work while balancing the needs of the business and individuals. When you join GE Appliances, you will have the opportunity to work with your leader to create a flexible work arrangement that balances the needs of the individual, team, and organization. 
 
 
 GE Appliances is an Equal Opportunity Employer.  Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. 
 
 GE Appliances participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality
identity_held_roles.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE:

The Senior Manager, Quality owns program quality end to end and leads the Quality Engineering team that supports it. You will build and lead a team of Quality Engineers across the program's process areas, owning requirements into our AS9100D quality management system, and be the single point of accountability for whether product is built to spec, on schedule, and with the objective quality evidence to prove it.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Team leadership — build, lead, and develop the Quality Engineering team supporting the project across sheet metal, welding and forming, NDT, foundry and forging, machining, and additive manufacturing.

• Staffing and coverage — close the open QE positions on the program, set priorities, and ensure every process area has quality coverage.

• Development and standards — coach QEs, set consistent standards of practice, and grow special-process competency (welding, NDT) across the team.

• Cross-functional partnership — represent quality with Build Engineering, Operations, and the program team, and serve as the escalation point for quality decisions on Nautilus.

• Program quality for Nautilus — first-article inspection (AS9102), product qualification, and quality across the build from receipt to delivery.

• Non-conformance and corrective action — control non-conforming material and customer escapes, drive root-cause and corrective action to closure, and own escape management for the program.

• Supplier and receiving quality — flow requirements to suppliers, verify certifications and OQE at receipt, and build receiving capability for controlled material.

• Audit readiness — prepare for and lead customer, and AS9100 audits for the program, and own the internal-audit posture that keeps it compliant.

• Metrics and reporting — quality KPIs, escape trends, and program quality status to leadership.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

• 8+ years in quality within defense, marine, nuclear, or aerospace manufacturing, including direct people-management of a quality team.

• Proven command of AS9100 / ISO 9001 and hands-on experience integrating customer and regulatory requirements into a QMS.

• Track record building quality processes and teams in a fast-scaling or startup manufacturing environment.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance; U.S. person under ITAR.



What Will Set You Apart

• Background at a submarine prime or shipyard (e.g., General Dynamics Electric Boat, HII Newport News) or a qualified SUBSAFE supplier.

• Knowledge of NAVSEA and SUBSAFE / Material Level I requirements (objective quality evidence, controlled material, traceability, cleanliness).

• AS9100 / ISO 9001 lead-auditor certification; familiarity with welding and NDT special-process controls (Nadcap).

• CQE, CMQ/OE, or equivalent quality certification.

• Experience standing up program quality from the ground up — writing the system, not just running it.




BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
 401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

identity_held_roles.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.



Commissioning Chief Engineer, Marauder

Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing defense autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.

Job Summary:

In this role you will be responsible for the commissioning and operation of the engine room and all associated machinery aboard a novel autonomous vessel. You will ensure that all marine systems — including but not limited to main propulsion, auxiliary machinery, fuel oil, lubrication, cooling, and associated environmental equipment — are properly tested and validated through structured commissioning processes and integrated with the vessel's autonomy and software control systems to support reliable manned, remote, and autonomous operation.

identity_held_roles.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




POSITION OVERVIEW

The Staff Quality Engineer serves as the VP of Quality's senior technical quality expert responsible for driving multi-site RCCA culture, supporting engineering and manufacturing quality. Reporting directly to the VP of Quality, this role leads enterprise-wide technical investigations, drives engineering-based Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA), and partners across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Product, and Mission Operations to improve product reliability and operational performance.

This position applies deep engineering expertise to identify fundamental technical failure mechanisms, validate corrective actions through engineering analysis and testing, and eliminate systemic product and process risks.

The Staff Quality Engineer operates across multiple manufacturing sites and product lines, working with cross functional teams on design opportunities, manufacturing processes, and operational readiness while establishing best practices for technical problem solving across the enterprise.




TECHNICAL PROBLEM SOLVING

 - Apply structured engineering methodologies to determine true physical, process, software, or systems root causes—not simply procedural gaps.

 - Utilize advanced analytical tools including Fault Tree Analysis, Fishbone, 5 Why, Statistical Analysis, Tolerance Stack Analysis, and FMEA.

 - Validate corrective actions using engineering data, experimentation, testing, and verification.

 - Drive permanent corrective actions that eliminate recurrence across products and manufacturing sites.




MULTI-SITE QUALITY LEADERSHIP

 - Provide technical quality leadership across multiple manufacturing locations.

 - Standardize RCCA methodologies and engineering investigations across the enterprise.

 - Coach site Quality Engineers on advanced engineering problem solving.

 - Lead enterprise technical reviews for recurring issues and customer escapes.

 - Support rapid problem escalation and recovery during production interruptions.




ROOT CAUSE & CORRECTIVE ACTION (RCCA)

 - Lead enterprise RCCA for manufacturing defects, supplier escapes, customer returns, field failures, and reliability issues.

 - Ensure investigations identify technical root causes rather than symptoms.




MANUFACTURING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT

 - Improve manufacturing capability through engineering analysis.

 - Reduce defects through process optimization rather than increased inspection.

 - Support New Product Introduction (NPI) Quality activities across multiple product lines.




CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Program Management, Product Management, Mission Operations, and Executive Leadership.

 - Present technical findings and recommendations to cross functional teams.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical or aerospace engineering.

 - 10+ years of engineering aerospace, defense, automotive, or advanced manufacturing.

 - Demonstrated success solving complex engineering problems.

 - Extensive experience leading engineering-based RCCA.

 - Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations.

 - Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.

 - Must be able to travel 30-50% of the time.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Design and development engineering management experience




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Establish an enterprise technical RCCA methodology across all manufacturing sites.

 - Reduce quality escapes through permanent corrective actions.

 - Improve manufacturing FPY.

 - Mentor Quality Engineers in advanced engineering problem solving.




BENEFITS

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with company match

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Pet Insurance: Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

identity_held_roles.title: Director, Product Quality
identity_held_roles.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 We are looking for a hands-on, high-impact Director, Product Quality  to lead our Field Quality and Failure Analysis engineering teams. In this role, you will hold ultimate accountability for overall field quality, reliability performance, and fleet health across all deployed commercial products. 

 You are a seasoned practitioner of rigorous problem-solving methodologies (8D, 5-Why, DMAIC) with a proven track record of diving deep into complex electromechanical, hardware, and firmware failures. You will bridge the gap between field service operations, customer sites, supplier quality, and internal product design teams to ensure field issues are contained rapidly, root-caused definitively, and prevented permanently. 

 About the Work 

 
 Own Field Quality & Fleet Health: Establish, monitor, and report on key field quality metrics (e.g., MTBI, MTTF, ARR, issue escape rates, service ticket turnaround time) for all shipping products and customer deployments. 

 Lead Failure Analysis (FA) & CAPA: Lead and grow a dedicated team of Failure Analysis Engineers. Drive rigorous Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) processes for field returns, hardware bugs, and system-level failures. 

 Field Containment & Rapid Response: Establish immediate containment protocols for critical field escalations, safety events, and unexpected fleet-wide failure trends to minimize customer downtime. 

 Cross-Functional Feedback Loop: Serve as the critical bridge between Field Operations, Customer Success, Hardware Engineering, Software/Firmware, and Supplier Quality. Drive design-for-reliability (DFR) feedback directly into next-generation product engineering. 

 Manage Closed-Loop Quality Systems: Implement and maintain robust Closed-Loop Corrective Action (CAPA) tracking across multi-site field deployments and repair depots. 

 Executive Communication & Governance: Host regular Field Quality Reviews with leadership, presenting objective data, failure Pareto analyses, root-cause findings, and measurable CAPA progress. 

 
 About You 

 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. 

 Experience: 10+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Field Quality, or Reliability Engineering within high-complexity hardware industries (Robotics, Automotive/EV, Aerospace, Autonomous Systems, or Complex Industrial Equipment). 

 Leadership: 5+ years of direct people management experience leading technical engineering teams (FA, Quality, or Sustaining Engineering). 

 Hands-on Expertise: Deep, practical experience executing physical failure analysis on electromechanical systems (actuators, harnesses, sensors, PCBAs, battery management systems, and precision mechanical linkages). 

 Methodologies: Certified or expert practitioner in structured root cause analysis tools (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa, Fault Tree Analysis, FMEA, Gauge R&R). 

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Advanced Degree: Master’s degree in Engineering Management or an Engineering discipline. 

 Certifications: Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE), or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt. 

 Domain Experience: Experience managing field reliability for autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), humanoid robotics, or safety-critical industrial equipment. 

 Systems Exposure: Familiarity firmware diagnostic tools, and telemetry data analytics for remote fleet diagnostics. 

 
 Work Environment & Travel 

 
 Position is based out of our Salem, OR facility with regular access to testing labs, service centers, and assembly lines. 

 Occasional travel (up to 20%) to customer sites, field test locations, or primary suppliers may be required to investigate critical quality escapes. 

 
 
 Location 

 
 This is an onsite position at our Salem, OR office. 

 
 The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Agility Robotics is a multi-state employer and this salary range may not reflect positions who work in other locations. These ranges may be modified in the future. 
 Anticipated Base Salary Range
 $162,000 — $210,000 USD 


 In addition to base pay, our competitive total rewards package consists of the following for full-time employees: 

 
 401(k) Plan:   Includes a 6% company match.

 Equity:   Company stock options.

 Insurance Coverage:   100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, and short/long-term disability insurance for employees.

 Benefit Start Date:   Eligible for benefits on your first day of employment.

 Well-Being Support:   Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

 Time Off: 
 
 Exempt Employees:   Flexible, unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown.

 Non-Exempt Employees:   10 vacation days, paid sick leave, and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown, annually.

 


 On-Site Perks:   Catered lunches four times a week and a variety of healthy snacks and refreshments at our Salem and Pittsburgh locations.

 Parental Leave:   Generous paid parental leave programs.

 Work Environment:   A culture that supports flexible work arrangements.

 Growth Opportunities:   Professional development and tuition reimbursement programs.

 Relocation Assistance:   Provided for eligible roles.

 Annual Discretionary Bonus: Provided for eligible roles.

 
 All of our roles are U.S.-based. Applicants must have current authorization to work in the United States. 

 Agility Robotics is committed to a work environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Each individual has the right to work in a professional atmosphere that promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits unlawful discriminatory practices, including harassment. Therefore, it is the policy of Agility Robotics to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, national origin, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Agility Robotics prohibits any such discrimination or harassment. 

  

 Agility Robotics does not accept unsolicited referrals from third-party recruiting agencies.  We prioritize direct applicants and encourage all qualified candidates to apply directly through our careers page.  If you are represented by a third party, your application may not be considered.  To ensure full consideration, please apply directly.

identity_held_roles.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

 OUR MISSION 

 True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

 OUR VALUES 

 
 Be the offset.   We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

 What would it take?  We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

 It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

 
 BENEFITS & PERKS *

 
 Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options

 Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave

 Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees

 And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays

 Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

 
 *Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

 YOUR MISSION: 

 At True Anomaly, production is a strategic advantage. Our ability to rapidly build, integrate, test, and deliver high-performance systems at scale is critical to mission success and long-term competitiveness.

 As Vice President of Production, you will build our production organization into a high-rate, quality focused build and test machine.  You will drive vertical integration to achieve pace and cost targets while developing automation and test infrastructure to support lights out verification across multiple product lines and mission sets. You will own manufacturing, assembly/integration, EGSE design and production, quality, and test and test automation — building the operational systems, infrastructure, and teams required to scale efficiently without compromising quality or speed.

 This role is responsible for creating a data-driven production organization that continuously improves throughput, reliability, and cost while enabling rapid iteration and delivery across the business.

 Key Responsibilities 

 
 Lead all manufacturing, assembly, integration, and production test operations across the company’s product lines while supporting prototyping for research and development.

 Develop and execute the production strategy required to scale from development programs into repeatable, high-rate manufacturing.

 Own the operational execution of the company’s vertical integration efforts, including standing up internal manufacturing and test capabilities for propulsion systems, fluid systems, PCBAs, FlatSats, RF systems, and integrated space vehicles.

 Build scalable production systems, workflows, and operational infrastructure that improve throughput, quality, and delivery performance across complex hardware production environments.

 Drive implementation of lean manufacturing principles, automation, and data-driven operational management across production environments supporting spacecraft, missile defense, and mission-critical component and payload systems.

 Own development and deployment of production tooling, EGSE, fixtures, and automated test systems required to support scalable manufacturing, integration, and environmental test operations.

 Partner closely with Engineering teams to drive design-for-manufacturing and design-for-test principles into product development.

 Establish production metrics, dashboards, and operational review processes focused on cycle time, yield, labor efficiency, throughput, and cost reduction.

 Lead quality execution across manufacturing, integration, inspection, RF test, propulsion test, and production verification activities, ensuring quality is embedded into operational processes.

 Drive automation of test execution, production data collection, and operational reporting to improve repeatability, traceability, and decision-making.

 Collaborate with Supply Chain, Engineering, Facilities, Security, and Program Management to ensure aligned production readiness and execution across both classified and unclassified production environments.

 Build and mentor high-performing teams capable of supporting rapid company growth and operational scale.

 Support long-term facility, staffing, secure manufacturing, and production capacity planning to meet future mission demand.

 
 Required Qualifications 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or related technical field

 15+ years of experience leading manufacturing, production, integration, or operations organizations in complex technical industries

 Proven experience scaling production operations from development into repeatable manufacturing environments

 Strong background in manufacturing, assembly/integration, production test, and operational execution for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems

 Experience standing up vertically integrated manufacturing or test capabilities across areas such as propulsion systems, fluid systems, PCBAs, RF systems, or integrated vehicle production

 Demonstrated success driving operational excellence, quality improvement, and cost reduction initiatives

 Experience implementing data-driven manufacturing systems, KPIs, and production management processes

 Strong understanding of design-for-manufacturing, production scaling, environmental test, and test automation principles

 Experience operating within high-complexity manufacturing environments

 Proven ability to lead large multidisciplinary teams in fast-paced, highly technical environments

 Excellent cross-functional leadership and communication skills

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Experience in aerospace, defense, launch vehicle, missile defense, or high-rate hardware manufacturing environments

 Familiarity with propulsion manufacturing and test operations, including additive manufacturing / 3D printing processes

 Experience with spacecraft integration and environmental test campaigns

 Familiarity with classified manufacturing and secure production operations

 Experience supporting rapid production scaling across multiple product lines

 Background implementing lean manufacturing or continuous improvement frameworks at scale

 Experience with automated manufacturing, MES, or production data systems

 Experience building operational organizations during periods of rapid company growth

 
 Compensation   

 
 Base Salary: $300,000 - $350,000 

 
 
 Equity + Benefits  including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO, and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave   

 
 Additional Requirements   

 
 Work Location – We observe an in-person work environment, and expect 4 days per week in office at the Company's Denver, CO headquarters or at our facility in Long Beach, California. 

 
 
 Security Clearance – Ability to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI clearance required. 

 
 This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below. 

  
 To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

 True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.

 To protect candidates and our company from application fraud and impersonation, we use third-party tools to verify applicant identity and detect fraudulent applications. Learn more in our Privacy Notice .

identity_held_roles.title: Head of Bedrock Operations Center
identity_held_roles.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Head of Bedrock Operations Center (BOC) to build and lead the central, always-on hub that oversees our deployed autonomous machines. As the Bedrock System deployments scale across new states, new machine types, and a next-generation platform, the BOC is how we keep every machine safe, productive, and supported around the clock.

This role owns three core functions: Remote Assistance, supporting autonomous machines in real time when they need a human decision; Customer & Partner Support, the single front door for customers, partners, and field teams; and Central Operations, which provides live visibility, dispatch coordination, and incident coordination and command.

The Head of BOC owns the Operations Center's operating model, organization, tooling requirements, performance, and manpower oversight. The BOC is accountable for the safe remote operations, uptime, and responsiveness our customers experience. Reporting to the VP of Operations, this leader is a critical thought partner to Product and to Operations Leads across the company.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Operations Center Strategy & Build-out

 - Define the BOC operating model, org structure, and coverage model (shifts, time zones, follow-the-sun) as the fleet scales

 - Build and lead the BOC leadership team and a growing workforce of shift leads and specialists

 - Own workforce planning and ensure adequate, qualified staffing; Partner with Product and Engineering on machines-per-operator ratios against fleet growth, product mix, and new machine types

 - Own the physical and technical readiness of the Operations Center, including infrastructure, redundancy, connectivity, and business continuity

Remote Assistance

 - Own round-the-clock remote operations for autonomous machines, including response-time SLAs, escalation protocols, and clear decision authority

 - Establish safety-first standards for remote interventions, remote stops, and hand-offs to on-site personnel, in partnership with Safety teams

 - Build training, certification, and quality-assurance programs for remote assistance operators

 - Analyze intervention data and partner with Autonomy Engineering to reduce interventions and improve machine autonomy over time

Customer & Partner Support

 - Build and lead a tiered support function (L1 / L2 / L3) with clear escalation paths into Field Operations, Service, Hardware, RA, and/ or Engineering

 - Define and deliver support SLAs tailored to each product line and customer commitment

 - Own ticketing, knowledge base, and customer communication standards; turn voice-of-customer trends into fixes

 - Partner with the Commercial team on customer onboarding, service commitments, and account health

Central Operations / Command & Control

 - Own live, fleet-wide situational awareness: machine status, health, location, and utilization across every site

 - Coordinate daily dispatch, service, and maintenance with Field Operations, including parts and technician routing

 - Serve as incident command for operational and safety events, with clear playbooks for triage, escalation, communication, and post-incident review

 - Own runbooks, shift hand-off standards, and change management for new sites, new machine types, and new platforms

Performance & Analytics

 - Define and track core BOC metrics: intervention rate and response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, fleet uptime, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to leadership

 - Lead continuous improvement through process, automation, and data, increasing the number of machines each operator can safely support


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Autonomous machines get fast, safe human support whenever they need it

 - Customers and partners have one clear front door and consistently fast resolution

 - Real-time visibility into every machine and site, with incidents handled calmly and transparently

 - Machines-per-operator rises steadily as intervention insights drive autonomy improvements

 - The Operations Center scales ahead of fleet growth, new sites, and new machine types without a drop in service


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - 12+ years in operations leadership, including 5+ years building and leading 24/7 or mission-critical operations (command centers, remote operations, network or fleet operations, or large-scale support organizations)

 - Experience building an operations organization from early stage to scale, including hiring and developing managers and shift leads and managing large hourly and/or contract workforces

 - Track record defining and managing SLAs, escalation paths, and incident response in safety-critical or high-availability environments

 - Experience influencing engineering, product, and commercial leaders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth

 - Strong analytical skills; comfortable with operational data, dashboards, and forecasting models (SQL / BI tools a plus)

 - Experience with workforce planning, scheduling, and shift-based operations

 - Excellent written and verbal communication with customers, field crews, and executives

Preferred

 - Experience running operations centers for autonomous vehicles, robotics, trucking, aviation, or mining

 - Experience leading remote assistance, teleoperation, or fleet response teams for autonomous systems

 - Familiarity with heavy machinery and/or the construction industry

 - Experience building B2B or technical support for industrial equipment or hardware products

 - Familiarity with fleet telemetry, monitoring and alerting, ticketing, and workforce-management tools

 - Experience launching operations across multiple regions or time zones

 - Continuous improvement / Lean / Six Sigma experience


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Every autonomous machine Bedrock deploys depends on the Operations Center to keep it safe, productive, and supported. You'll build the function that lets our fleet scale with confidence, and directly shape the experience every customer and partner has with Bedrock.

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.
