existing_roles.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

We're hiring our first Sr. Manager of Production Planning & Scheduling to own the factory side execution. Where our S&OP function decides where and whether we can build across the network, you own how and when it actually gets built on the floor. You'll own discrete operational scheduling, job sequencing and priority, and the daily/weekly rhythm that ensures on-time delivery (OTD) and sets the factory up for success.

This role reports to our Operations leadership and drives a consistent scheduling methodology across the network, while partnering closely with each site General Manager on execution. Your scheduling and planning team members will support the sites day-to-day (dotted-line to the GM) while you own the standards, methodology, and rigor centrally.

This is a builder and owner role. While the team is built out, you'll be hands-on developing the scheduling methodologies, communication rigor, and visual management that don't exist yet, and turning them into standard work. You'll be the person the floor, Program Management, and leadership rely on for a clear, credible answer to "what are we running, in what order, and are we going to hit the date?"

You'll partner tightly with the S&OP function, translating network-level allocation and capacity plans into an executable factory schedule — and feeding real execution signal back up to highlight and drive capacity improvements.

What You'll Do:

Own Production Scheduling & Execution

· Own discrete production scheduling and job sequencing across work centers to maximize on-time delivery and throughput.

· Own work order release to the floor and control what work is released and when.

· Set and manage priority and milestone dates, establish clear, transparent rules for what runs when, and make the trade-off calls when priorities conflict.

· Own data integrity for schedules and dates in the system, and maintain and drive accurate MRP schedules so plans, priorities, and downstream commitments can be trusted.

· Build the daily/weekly scheduling cadence and standard work that keeps the floor aligned, from shift-level execution to weekly look-ahead.

· Translate S&OP network allocation and capacity plans into an executable, sequenced factory schedule.

· Partner closely with the site General Manager to align on priorities, sequencing, and daily execution serving as the GM's right hand for turning the plan into on-time output.

· Establish the system and cadence for tracking work order progress through the floor, monitors status against milestone dates, surfaces at risk jobs early, and drives rapid recovery on exceptions.

Drive OTD & Factory Performance

 - Own on time delivery as a primary metric track it, root cause misses, and close the gaps.

 - Ensure the factory is set up for success: materials, tooling, capacity, and priorities aligned ahead of the work, not discovered at the machine.

 - Highlight and drive capacity improvements — surface constraints and bottlenecks from real execution data and partner with Operations and Engineering to resolve them.

 - Feed execution signal (actual cycle times, constraints, attainment) back to S&OP to sharpen capacity models and sellable-capacity commitments.

Build Methodology, Rigor & Visibility

 - Develop the scheduling methodologies and logic from the ground up, sequencing rules, buffering, prioritization frameworks and codify them as standard work applied consistently across sites.

 - Establish communication rigor: the meeting cadence, escalation paths, and reporting that keep the floor, the GMs, and leadership on the same page.

 - Build the visual management schedules, boards, dashboards, and status views that make factory status, priorities, and risks obvious at a glance.

 - Establish key scheduling metrics: OTD, schedule adherence, past due, work center utilization, and cycle time performance.

People Leadership

 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of production planners and schedulers as the function scales, including team members embedded at and dotted lined to the sites.

 - Build organizational capability through talent development, standard work, training, and performance management.

 - Foster a culture of accountability, urgency, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

· Proven experience in production planning, scheduling, or shop floor operations management in a discrete manufacturing environment.

· Deep understanding of production scheduling, sequencing, priority management, master scheduling, capacity/constraint analysis, and OTD drivers.

· Hands on experience with scheduling/ERP/MES systems and strong analytical and data visualization skills.

· Experience leading teams and developing planning/scheduling talent.

· Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to drive urgency and accountability on the floor.

· ERP/MRP expertise work order lifecycle, MRP mechanics, and maintaining schedule/date data integrity at scale.

Education & Experience Requirements

 - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, Finance, or related discipline preferred.

 - 5+ years of progressive experience in production planning, scheduling, or manufacturing operations.


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



Role Summary

The Director, Forward Deployed Engineering leads the technical arm of Hadrian's Customer Programs motion. You sit inside Build Engineering and partner directly with the Customer Programs team, owning the manufacturing scoping of new customer engagements: translating what a customer wants into what Hadrian will actually commit to and build.

This role works directly with customers every day. For many of them, you and your team are the face of Hadrian engineering, so how you show up in the room matters as much as the technical answer. The work starts with discovery. Before anything is proposed, you and your team get inside the customer's operation: observing how work actually flows, mapping their processes and constraints, and interviewing the people closest to the problem until you understand what they need, which is often different from what they first ask for.

From there, you shape a solution that maximizes what the customer gets out of the engagement and builds toward where Hadrian is headed. The craft is steering to the answer where the customer's best outcome and Hadrian's direction reinforce each other: high impact, low effort, and built on what we already do well rather than new obligations we then have to invent our way out of.

The intent behind housing this role in Build Engineering is clean accountability: your team scopes what we commit to, and Build Engineering delivers it. That means the commitments you shape have to be grounded in first-principles engineering judgment and a real understanding of the factory, not optimism. You evaluate and understand before you propose or promise.


Key Responsibilities

 - Represent Hadrian with customers day to day: Own the technical relationship with customer engineering, program, and leadership teams. Run working sessions, present findings and recommendations, handle hard questions and pushback in the room, and follow up with clear, accurate written communication. Every interaction should leave the customer more confident in Hadrian.

 - Discover before you design: Embed with customers to observe their operations, map processes, constraints, and pain points, and interview stakeholders from the shop floor to program leadership. Build a clear, evidence-based picture of the real need before any solution is on the table.

 - Shape the solution: Fold what you learn into a solution that maximizes customer output and moves Hadrian toward what we are building. Hold an accurate picture of current capability and roadmap, and steer each engagement to the point where those two goals reinforce each other, favoring existing capabilities over new obligations.

 - Partner with Customer Programs: Operate on a dotted line to Customer Programs as their forward deployed engineering arm, bringing technical judgment into every engagement from first conversation through commitment.

 - Lead the forward deployed engineering team: Build, manage, and develop a technical team that engages directly with customers during new program scoping. Set the standard for how the team runs discovery, evaluates opportunities, and communicates with customers in a technical, credible, low-ego way.

 - Scope new customer engagements: Own the manufacturing scoping of new engagements: review requirements, drawings, specifications, tolerances, materials, and volumes, and define a manufacturing solution that Hadrian can commit to with confidence.

 - Evaluate before you promise: Bring a first-principles engineering mindset to every engagement. Understand the problem and the constraints before proposing or committing to a solution, so that what we sign up for is real and deliverable.

 - Hand off cleanly to Build Engineering: Ensure every commitment is scoped so that the Build Engineering organization can deliver it: clear product definition, make-vs-buy posture, process capability requirements, and a manufacturing plan that stands up to execution.

 - Drive leverage, not one-offs: Recognize recurring customer patterns and turn them into repeatable scoping approaches and reusable solution templates, so the function scales with the business instead of scaling headcount linearly.
   

Required Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field and 8+ years of manufacturing or manufacturing engineering experience, or 12+ years of that experience without a degree.

 - 3+ years managing technical teams (direct reports).

 - Experience in a customer-facing technical role (e.g., applications, field or sales engineering, program engineering, or consulting), including presenting technical recommendations to customer engineering and program leadership.

 - Proven ability to lead a technical team in a customer-facing capacity, translating between customer requirements and manufacturing reality.

 - Demonstrated ability to run structured customer discovery (site visits, process mapping, stakeholder interviews) and turn it into a defined technical solution.

 - Strong first-principles engineering judgment: able to evaluate and understand complex requirements before proposing or committing to solutions.

 - Fluency reading and interpreting engineering drawings, specifications, GD&T, and manufacturing process requirements.

 - Experience scoping or defining manufacturing work: DFM, make-vs-buy, process planning, tooling strategy, or production launch.
   

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience in aerospace, defense, maritime, or other high-complexity, high-mix manufacturing environments.

 - Background spanning both a scaling/startup environment and a mature manufacturing organization.

 - Exposure to precision machining, castings, forgings, sheet metal, or additive processes across metals and composites.

 - Experience working alongside sales, program management, or commercial teams on new customer engagements.

 - Exposure to manufacturing software and automation (MES/ERP, CAM automation, robotics, factory data systems), with a track record of feeding what you learn from customers back into product and automation roadmaps so those capabilities get built ahead of demand.

 - A track record of building repeatable systems and templates rather than solving each problem from scratch.


BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. existing_roles.title: Vice President of Operations
existing_roles.description:
Quindar builds software to manage satellites like servers. We are seeking a Vice President of Operations to build the operating system, organizational infrastructure, and business processes that turn company strategy into execution as we scale across commercial and government markets.

This leader owns business operations, strategy and performance, facilities, and General & Administrative functions. Beyond running the operating cadence, the role connects corporate strategy, resource allocation, and cross-functional execution so that Quindar consistently makes the right investments and turns them into business outcomes. The role holds the authority to resolve cross-functional prioritization conflicts at the leadership level, with clear and intentional escalation to the CEO, while functional leaders retain accountability for their results and authority over their teams.

Facilities, Business Operations, and the G&A team report to this role, with their leaders responsible for day-to-day execution. This is a hands-on executive role for someone who can build a function, develop its leaders, and drive execution across the company.



Company Execution and Performance Management

• Translate company strategy into company OKRs and functional commitments with accountable owners, deadlines, dependencies, and approved resources.

• Agree with each functional leader on a small set of meaningful KPIs with clear definitions, source data, targets, and reporting frequency, and maintain a consolidated performance dashboard across Sales, Product, Engineering, Programs, Finance, People and Brand, and Operations.

• Design and run the company operating model: quarterly planning, leadership reviews, decision tracking, and follow-up, with a visible record of commitments delivered, missed, corrected, and rescoped.

• Design and implement a company-wide model for cross-functional prioritization and decision-making at the leadership level, including decision rights and escalation paths, aligned with and actively reinforced by the CEO.

• Use the operating data to drive decisions and corrective actions, resolve cross-functional dependencies, and escalate decisions that put company goals at risk.

• Partner with functional leaders and the VP of Finance to align workforce capacity, hiring plans, facilities, and budgets with company priorities.



Corporate Strategy and Go-to-Market

• Help shape corporate strategy with the CEO and leadership team, including evaluating markets and opportunities, defining investment requirements, and translating strategic choices into resourced plans.

• Lead the cross-functional planning and execution of GTM priorities in partnership with the CEO, who leads Sales & Marketing: align Product, Engineering, Programs, and Operations behind revenue priorities and ensure the organization is resourced to deliver them.

• Lead the evaluation and incubation of new business opportunities, including, but not limited to,Operations as a Service (OaaS). For OaaS, lead the initial cross-functional effort to take the offering from concept toward launch, including the business model, service definition and commercial terms, investment requirements, and operational readiness.

• Ensure new services, markets, and programs are integrated into company planning, performance management, and compliance from the outset.



AI-Enabled Business Operations

• Lead the AI Business Operations team to build and deploy workflows that reduce manual coordination and increase output across Quindar, with measurable reductions in hands-on processing time and sustained adoption.

• Identify and baseline the highest-value workflows across functions, prioritizing those that remove coordination overhead between Product, Engineering, Programs, Sales, and Marketing (for example, specifications to engineering tickets, user documentation, marketing materials, and proposal development).

• Build internal knowledge infrastructure, such as a company data warehouse of product knowledge, engineering designs, documentation, and marketing and proposal content, that any role can query or use to create collateral through an agentic interface.

• Implement appropriate access controls, source traceability, and compliance requirements, including CUI handling, before any workflow handling sensitive or consequential outputs enters production use.



Facilities and Classified Readiness

• Own facilities planning, buildouts, workplace operations, vendor management, and procurement across all unclassified and classified spaces.

• Maintain an integrated master schedule covering construction, procurement, vendors, budget, and readiness for each space, with a defined risk and impact scale, reviewed regularly with the CEO.

• Deliver the facilities infrastructure needed for classified readiness, completing facilities work ahead of accreditation target dates and obtaining Security’s written acceptance against an agreed readiness checklist.

• Partner with Security, IT, Contracts, and program leadership so that facilities, policies, training, and records support classified program and audit requirements. Security retains accreditation responsibility.



General and Administrative Operations

• Lead legal operations, and corporate administrative services through internal teams and outside partners.

• Manage outside counsel and coordinate corporate legal matters, employment matters, contract review, and company policies.

• Own cap table and stock option administration in partnership with Finance and legal counsel, and maintain corporate records and board and stockholder approval workflows with the CEO and counsel.

• Own the administrative infrastructure required to pursue and support government business, including SAM.gov http://SAM.gov registration, applicable NSTXL and consortium memberships, JCP certification/DD Form 2345, and a centralized calendar of registrations, renewals, and reporting obligations.

• Oversee export compliance program administration, including applicable ITAR/EAR processes, working with qualified counsel and designated compliance personnel.

• Coordinate corporate insurance, business continuity planning, corporate overhead efficiency, and company-wide operational risk management.



Fundraising and Finance Partnership

• Lead operational, legal, people, and corporate diligence readiness for fundraising alongside the VP of Finance, including an organized data room and timely, accurate responses to investor requests.

• Support board materials and investor reporting with company operating metrics, organizational plans, and progress against strategic priorities.

• Partner with Finance on operating plans, overhead budgets, and the investments needed to support the next stage of growth and new business lines.



Qualifications

• Experience leading operations at a growing technology company, with exposure to government contracting or another regulated market.

• Demonstrated success building teams, systems, and operating processes through a significant stage of organizational growth.

• Experience contributing to corporate strategy and leading cross-functional GTM or new-business initiatives from concept to launch, with a bias toward revenue and business outcomes.

• Experience across facilities, legal operations, compliance, or business operations.

• A hands-on track record of using AI, technology, and automation to improve operational efficiency.

• Familiarity with venture-backed company governance, equity administration, and fundraising diligence.

• Ability to turn ambiguous priorities into clear plans, coordinate executive peers, and hold teams accountable for commitments.

• Strong judgment about when to act directly, delegate, escalate, or engage specialist expertise.



What Success Looks Like

• Company strategy is reflected in OKRs, KPIs, and commitments with clear owners, and leaders run the business from a trusted, shared dashboard.

• Cross-functional prioritization decisions are made quickly and consistently at the leadership level, with less day-to-day intervention from the CEO.

• GTM priorities and new services such as OaaS move from strategy to resourced, cross-functionally executed plans with measurable revenue impact.

• AI-enabled workflows are in production across functions, materially reducing manual coordination while meeting access-control and compliance requirements.

• Facilities for classified operations are delivered on schedule and accepted by Security.

• Organizational structures, career frameworks, equity programs, and scaling processes are ready ahead of growth to 150+ employees.

• Required registrations, compliance obligations, and corporate and equity records remain current and diligence-ready.



Security Clearance Eligibility Requirement
Due to U.S. Government contractual requirements, this position requires eligibility for a U.S. Government security clearance. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance; therefore, candidates for this position must be U.S. citizens. An active clearance is not required at the time of hire but is preferred and may be required in the future based on program needs.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

 - To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/ddtc_public/ddtc_public?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.


WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING AT QUINDAR

 - We work in a cutting edge industry and you will get the opportunity to be part of a small team with a large direct impact on the success of our customers’ space missions!

 - We take work life balance very seriously. We require employees to take 15 days off but provide unlimited PTO and follow most US federal government holidays.

 - Mental health is just as important as physical so we provide quarterly health & wellness benefits.

 - Comprehensive health insurance for you and your family with 100% coverage for employees.

 - We encourage employees to save for retirement and provide 4% 401(k) matching.

 - Each quarter we have a 4-day company offsite. Previous locations include San Francisco, Nashville, Denver, Santa Fe, New Orleans, San Diego, Bozeman, and New York City.

 - Our culture and company is evolving. You will be key in creating the next major or minor version!

existing_roles.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Head of Manufacturing Engineering to lead the development and scale-up of our manufacturing systems for high-volume small unmanned aircraft production. This leader will own the manufacturing engineering organization responsible for translating product designs into robust, automated, production-ready manufacturing systems capable of operating reliably at scale.

A major focus of this role will be factory automation, controls engineering, equipment development, and manufacturing systems architecture. You will build and lead a multidisciplinary organization spanning manufacturing engineering, automation and controls, equipment engineering, process development, and production industrialization.

The ideal candidate has experience scaling complex electromechanical products from early production into high-rate manufacturing, with a strong understanding of how automation, controls, data, equipment design, and process engineering come together to create a world-class production system.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can establish the long-term manufacturing strategy while also driving execution on the factory floor.



How You’ll Make an Impact:

 - Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Manufacturing Engineering organization supporting production from new product introduction through high-volume manufacturing.

 - Define the manufacturing engineering strategy, technical roadmap, organizational structure, and capabilities required to support significant production growth.

 - Partner closely with Design Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Test Engineering, and Product teams to ensure products are designed for manufacturability, automation, testability, and scale.

 - Establish manufacturing standards, design reviews, equipment specifications, process qualification methodologies, and production-readiness criteria.

 - Lead the architecture, development, deployment, and lifecycle management of automated manufacturing equipment and production systems.

 - Build strong internal capabilities in controls engineering, PLC programming, industrial robotics, motion control, machine vision, industrial networking, sensors, servo systems, safety systems, and automated material handling.

 - Establish controls and automation standards that enable equipment to be deployed, supported, replicated, and scaled rapidly across production.

 - Develop strategies for balancing manual, semi-automated, and fully automated manufacturing based on production rate, process capability, economics, and product maturity.

 - Establish disciplined equipment development processes including requirements definition, design reviews, FAT/SAT, commissioning, process validation, and production acceptance.

 - Partner with external automation integrators and equipment suppliers while developing critical automation and controls capabilities internally.

 - Build a highly instrumented manufacturing environment where equipment and processes generate actionable production data.

 - Partner with software and data teams to connect manufacturing equipment with MES, traceability, quality, and factory data systems.

 - Develop automated collection and analysis of process parameters, equipment states, cycle times, downtime, quality results, and genealogy.

 - Use manufacturing data to identify process drift, predict failures, improve yield, and accelerate root-cause analysis.



What Makes You a Good Fit:

 - 12+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, automation engineering, controls engineering, equipment engineering, or related disciplines.

 - 5+ years of experience leading engineering organizations responsible for manufacturing systems or factory automation.

 - Demonstrated experience scaling complex electromechanical products into high-volume production.

 - Experience in aerospace, automotive, robotics, industrial automation, electronics, battery, semiconductor, or another highly engineered manufacturing environment; aerospace experience strongly preferred.

 - Deep understanding of manufacturing automation and controls, including several of the following:
   
   - PLC and industrial controls architectures
   
   - Robotics and robotic cells
   
   - Servo and motion-control systems
   
   - Machine vision
   
   - Industrial networking and communications
   
   - Sensors and instrumentation
   
   - Automated test and inspection
   
   - Machine safety systems
   
   - SCADA/HMI systems
   
   - Manufacturing equipment software

 - Experience developing custom production equipment from concept through production deployment.

 - Experience developing capital equipment strategies and managing significant CapEx programs.

 - Strong understanding of DFM/DFA and the ability to influence product architecture to enable manufacturing scale and automation.

 - Experience operating in environments requiring rigorous configuration management, traceability, process control, and quality systems.

 - Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, and lead multidisciplinary technical organizations.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to move between factory-level strategy and detailed engineering problems.

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related technical field.

 - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.



Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience scaling aerospace or similarly complex hardware from low-rate initial production to hundreds or thousands of units per month.

 - Experience building an automation and controls engineering function from the ground up.

 - Experience designing manufacturing systems for products combining mechanical assemblies, electronics, motors, sensors, batteries, composites, or other complex electromechanical technologies.

 - Familiarity with aerospace manufacturing and quality frameworks such as AS9100.

 - Experience with MES, equipment connectivity, manufacturing data infrastructure, and Industry 4.0 architectures.

 - Experience with automated inspection, machine vision, robotic assembly, dispensing, fastening, material handling, or automated test systems.

 - Experience developing standardized automation platforms that can be replicated across multiple production lines or factories.

 - Experience working in fast-growth hardware organizations where product design and manufacturing systems evolve simultaneously.

 - Master's degree in an engineering discipline or equivalent technical experience.



Compensation: At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $196,000 - $257,000*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. existing_roles.title: Head of Supply Chain & Manufacturing Strategy
existing_roles.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Skydio is committed to becoming a world class manufacturing company. U.S. policy is moving toward secure, domestic drone supply chains and evolving policy on component origin, supplier eligibility, market access and import duties are raising the bar for every manufacturer in the industry. Skydio has historically been at the forefront of investing in US manufacturing and blue supply, and we are doubling down on our commitments to ensure America leads the next frontier of flight. This role will drive the strategic plan to build the drone manufacturing mecca and the stable and compliant supply chains that feed it.




BUILDING ON A HEAD START

Skydio is the largest U.S.-based drone manufacturer, and we have treated secure supply chains as a strategic investment from the start. All of our current drone solutions, including X10, Dock for X10 and R10, are on the Blue UAS Cleared List. We have outgrown four U.S. manufacturing facilities in eight years. In April 2026 we committed $3.5 billion over five years to expand U.S. manufacturing through our SkyForge initiative, R&D and supply chain development. That includes a new U.S. factory five times the size of our current space and directing more than $1 billion to domestic suppliers. Through SkyForge, select suppliers will co-locate production with Skydio and work alongside our engineers, expanding and in some cases starting domestic manufacturing of critical parts. You will spearhead the SkyForge initiative and help decide where that investment goes and make sure it pays off: which components to onshore first, which suppliers to develop, and which capabilities to bring in-house.

Skydio is committed to becoming a world class manufacturing company. U.S. policy is moving toward secure, domestic drone supply chains and evolving policy on component origin, supplier eligibility, market access and import duties are raising the bar for every manufacturer in the industry. Skydio has historically been at the forefront of investing in US manufacturing and blue supply,  and we are doubling down on our commitments to ensure America leads the next frontier of flight . This role will drive the strategic plan to build the drone manufacturing mecca and the stable and compliant supply chains that feed it.




WHAT YOU'LL NAVIGATE

 - NDAA restrictions and the American Security Drone Act

 - The Blue UAS Cleared List and Blue UAS Framework

 - The DDP Supply Chain Framework and its phased component requirements

 - The FCC Covered List and equipment authorization

 - Section 232 tariffs and country-of-origin requirements




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Regulatory Partner: You will work closely with our regulatory team to understand current regulations, policy direction and will work directly with key partners setting this policy to help influence

 - Supply Chain and Manufacturing Strategy: Determine which capabilities and technologies we onshore, vertically integrate or partner on to build robust and compliant supply chains

 - Onshoring and supplier development: Set priorities for securing and onshoring supply across our critical commodities with the commodity teams. Where a domestic or allied supply base does not yet exist, decide whether to develop a supplier (including through SkyForge), bring the work in-house, or design around the constraint.

 - Make-versus-buy and vertical integration: Assess which production we should bring into our U.S. facilities and build the case with Manufacturing, Supply Chain and Finance. A well-supported recommendation against integration is as valuable as one for it.

 - Product compliance risk: Maintain a live, evidence-backed view of where each product line stands against each regulation. Translate it into schedule, revenue and cost terms the leadership team can act on, and report on a regular cadence.

 - Supplier-of-record decisions during design: Work alongside Global Supply Managers (GSMs) and hardware engineering during NPI to set SPOR. Bring the regulatory screen into design reviews early enough that engineering can still act on it.

 - Multi-tier traceability: Stand up bill-of-materials traceability to tier three and beyond, with country of origin and chain of custody, across purchased and in-house components.

 - Compliance and cost together: Find moves that serve compliance, tariff and domestic-content goals at once, and look for other opportunities to drive domestic sourcing to cost parity with traditional supply chains.
   
   


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

90 days: A complete risk baseline across products and regulations, separating hard blockers from cost problems, with named owners for every gap and a first readout to leadership.

3 months: An approved sourcing and supplier-development plan, a first vertical integration recommendation, and compliance screening built into design reviews. Each product line has a decided market-access pathway.

6 months: No launch is surprised by a compliance gap. Onshoring and supplier investments are prioritized by where they build the most durable advantage, and make-versus-buy decisions weigh compliance, tariff and domestic-content effects together.



WHAT YOU BRING


REQUIRED

 - 10+ years in supply chain, manufacturing operations, commodity management or operations strategy, including at least 3 in a regulated hardware environment where sourcing decisions carried legal or contractual consequences.

 - Experience influencing component and supplier selection during design, through NPI, design reviews, or SPOR and approved vendor list (AVL) decisions.

 - Credibility with both a sourcing organization and a factory. You can discuss capacity, tooling and yield as fluently as supplier qualification.

 - Accountable ownership of a multi-tier country-of-origin, supplier compliance or trade compliance program.

 - A make-versus-buy or vertical integration analysis you personally built and defended, including capex and ramp assumptions.

 - A track record of turning technical findings into executive decisions, and of changing engineering or sourcing decisions you had no formal authority over.

 - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.


PREFERRED

 - Working knowledge of NDAA §889/§848, country-of-origin and substantial-transformation analysis, Buy American domestic-content tests, or DFARS and FAR flow-downs

 - Background in in-house manufacturing, UAS, aerospace and defense, defense electronics, or EMS and contract manufacturing

 - Commodity experience in batteries and cells, motors and magnetics, imaging or thermal sensors, or PCB and PCBA

 - Experience standing up a production line or bringing an outsourced process in-house

 - Experience with a Blue UAS or Green UAS submission, or a DCMA or DCSA assessment

 - Experience developing domestic or allied-country suppliers from scratch




HOW THE ROLE FITS

 - Reports to: Head of Hardware Operations. Individual contributor at hire, with a path to building a small team as the program grows.

 - Peers: VP of Supply Chain and VP of Manufacturing.

 - Partners: Regulatory, Manufacturing Engineering, GSMs, Program Leads, Trade Compliance and Finance.

 - Visibility: Regular briefings to the leadership team on SkyForge progress. Several decisions this role informs are capital-allocation decisions.

existing_roles.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

About the Role:

The NPI Operations Engineering leader builds and leads the team responsible for making Skydio's next generation of autonomous robotics, including drones, docks and accessories, at our internal manufacturing facility in Hayward. You’ll deliver the process, manufacturing know-how and technology needed to build the most capable flying robots on the planet. The team combines Manufacturing Design Engineering and Supply Base Engineering into one organization that is 100% focused on new product development.

You will own the manufacturability of every new product: assembly time, assembly yield and the processes, fixtures, equipment and supplier readiness needed to hit them. You and your team will engage with Product Engineering from early architecture, carry products through EVT, DVT and PVT, and hand them to Process Engineering for sustaining once they meet clear production-readiness criteria.

This is a leadership role with significant scope to shape how Skydio develops hardware. You'll set the team's direction, hire and grow engineers, and be the single operations voice in product development. Sustaining engineering for products already in production sits with Process Engineering, so this team stays focused on getting new products right before they reach the line.



How You’ll Make an Impact:


OWN MANUFACTURABILITY OF NEW PRODUCTS

 - Own the operations engineering development for NPI programs across supply chain and in-house manufacturing

 - Drive design-for-manufacturing, assembly and serviceability (DFx) input from early architecture onward

 - Set and commit to assembly time and assembly yield targets for each new product, and track them at every build

 - Own operations sign-off at product development gates, and escalate manufacturability risks with clear trade-offs

 - Use PFMEA, DFM reviews and prototype yield, quality and process data to align product design with manufacturing strategy

 - Identify manufacturing risks early and drive mitigation plans to closure before production ramp


LEAD NPI EXECUTION THROUGH PRODUCTION READINESS

 - Own the manufacturing plan for new products and major design changes, from prototype through PVT

 - Define assembly flow, line layout, fixtures and equipment for new products, with labor, cost and capacity estimates that sharpen at each build

 - Coordinate engineering, design and production validation builds with Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Test and Quality

 - Define production-readiness and handoff criteria, and lead manufacturing readiness reviews

 - Develop and continuously improve Skydio's NPI process

 - Transfer products to Process Engineering with complete documentation, released tooling, and yield and cycle time at target


DEVELOP PROCESSES, FIXTURES AND ASSEMBLY EQUIPMENT

 - Own development and validation of assembly processes, including mechanical assembly, electronics integration, adhesive bonding, fastening, soldering and calibration

 - Own design and qualification of assembly fixtures, error-proofing, and assembly equipment such as dispense systems and torque-controlled drivers

 - Own the capital budget for new-product assembly fixtures and equipment. Capital for the running production line stays with Manufacturing

 - Develop process specifications, control plans, component and assembly CTQs, inspections, inline tests, work instructions and manufacturing BOMs, all complete before handoff

 - Use statistical process control (SPC), capability studies and structured experiments to establish robust process windows


DEVELOP CORE MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGIES

 - Build a roadmap of core process technologies that future products depend on, such as waterproofing and ingress protection, conformal coatings, sealing and advanced bonding

 - Partner with material suppliers, equipment vendors and technology partners to develop, qualify and industrialize these processes ahead of product need

 - Serve as the technical owner for these technologies after production launch


LEAD SUPPLY BASE ENGINEERING FOR NEW PRODUCTS

 - Drive supplier selection, part qualification and supplier process readiness for new products

 - Own NPI automation at the process level during development, and partner with the Factory Automation team for production handoff

 - Work with suppliers on component DFM, process capability, capacity and quality before production launch

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Quality on make-versus-buy decisions, supplier development and capital business cases


LEAD AND BUILD THE TEAM

 - Set the vision, strategy and execution plan for NPI Operations Engineering

 - Lead, hire and develop a team of manufacturing design engineers and supply base engineers, acting as the team's lead technical expert and mentor

 - Integrate MDE and SBE into one team with shared programs, goals and ways of working

 - Set priorities and staffing across multiple concurrent programs and SKUs at different stages, working with leaders across the company to understand build targets and focus the team on hitting them

 - Protect the team's focus on new products, with a clean handoff to Process Engineering for sustaining

 - Build an inclusive, diverse, engaged and high-performing team through a mix of external hiring and developing internal talent, with regular coaching and growth opportunities

 - Build a culture of technical rigor, ownership and close partnership with design engineering


COLLABORATION

 - Work closely with Product Engineering leaders on airframes, propulsion, cameras, sensors, batteries, gimbals and payloads

 - Align with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Test Engineering and Automation Engineering on capacity, equipment and handoff plans

 - Communicate program status, risks and manufacturability trade-offs clearly to executive leadership
   
   

What Makes You a Good Fit:

 - Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial or Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.

 - 10+ years of hands-on experience in manufacturing engineering, NPI or production engineering for complex electromechanical products, ideally including high-volume production.

 - [4+] years leading engineering teams, including hiring and developing engineers [and managers].

 - A track record of taking multiple complex hardware products from early development into high-quality production.

 - Deep expertise in DFM/DFA and a history of influencing product design early, not only fixing problems at the build.

 - Hands-on fixture design experience, and a strong understanding of factory lines, assembly flow and how to optimize them.

 - SPC, Lean and Six Sigma experience.

 - Experience working with suppliers on part qualification, process capability and production readiness.

 - Strong data skills: you set yield, cycle-time and cost targets, measure them and use the data to drive decisions.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, working collaboratively with people at every level, from technicians to executive leadership.

 - Strong project management, analytical skills and attention to detail, with sound independent judgment on complex, broad-scope problems.

 - Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with evolving products, and willingness to be on the floor during critical builds.

 - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with drones, aerospace, robotics, autonomous systems or consumer electronics.

 - Experience developing waterproofing and ingress-protection solutions (IP-rated products), conformal coating, sealing or adhesive processes.

 - Experience with PCBAs, cameras and optics, gimbals, inertial sensors, motors, batteries or composite structures.

 - Experience working with contract manufacturers or managing NPI across in-house and outsourced production.

existing_roles.title: VP of Mission Assurance & Quality (MA&Q)
existing_roles.description:
Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place!

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems.

We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life. 


The VP, Mission Assurance & Quality (MA&Q) holds the independent oversight authority that ensures every spacecraft is safe, reliable, and qualified before it launches. This role is structurally independent of all other VP organizations - the authority to halt work, reject deliverables, and withhold qualification sign-off cannot be overridden by any VP. Only the CTO can override an MA&Q determination, and that override is documented with the MA&Q position on record regardless of outcome.
 
Independence is the defining feature of this role. MA&Q does not build hardware, does not own schedule, and does not report to any VP who does. This structural separation is deliberate - quality and safety decisions must never be compromised by production pressure, schedule urgency, or cost targets.
 
The VP, MA&Q must be willing to halt a production line, delay a gate review, or withhold qualification sign-off when the evidence demands it - and hold that position under pressure from peers and the CTO alike.

What you’ll be doing:
Mission Assurance
Own the FMEA/FMECA from initial build through qualification -zero unmitigated single-point failures is a CDR entry criterion
Chair the Failure Review Board (FRB) -convene, lead root cause investigation, assess extent of condition, and close with verified corrective action
Define mission success criteria and own fault tree analysis
Safety
Implement and own the system safety program per MIL-STD-882 or program-equivalent standard
Lead hazard analysis (PHA, SHA) and maintain the hazard tracking log through every gate
Manage propulsion, battery, high-voltage, and deployment safety; provide range safety interface for launch operations
Quality Assurance
Exercise independent inspection authority across all program phases
Hold sole NCR disposition authority -Use-As-Is and Repair require MA&Q concurrence regardless of phase
Enforce workmanship standards per IPC-A-610 Class 3; conduct process audits and first article inspections
Issue Standing Disposition Authorizations (SDAs) for recurring Tier 2/3 NCRs; Tier 1 Critical NCRs trigger CTO notification within 4 hours
Reliability Engineering
Own quantitative reliability model per MIL-HDBK-217 or equivalent; track MTBF/MTTR targets against the constellation availability model
Lead reliability growth tracking, redundancy analysis, and reliability predictions correlated with test data at QR
Parts Engineering & Radiation
Maintain the Preferred Parts List (PPL) - sole authority to add or remove parts; no part may fly without PPL approval
Enforce derating compliance at CDR and manage lot acceptance testing
Specify the mission radiation environment (TID, SEE, displacement damage) and track radiation margins for all flight parts
Configuration Management
Chair the production CCB and administer the ECO/ECN process
Maintain as-built configuration records from the MES; execute FCA and PCA before Phase Close Gate
Provide as-built conformance report to the CTO
What you bring to this role:
15+ years of progressive mission assurance, quality engineering, or reliability engineering on flight programs; at least one spacecraft program carried from system requirements through on-orbit operations
Demonstrated record of exercising halt/reject authority or withholding qualification sign-off against schedule and cost pressure you must describe a specific instance. This is the most important qualification for the role
Direct accountability for a flight program's FMEA/FMECA from initial build through qualification, including enforcing zero-unmitigated-SPOF at CDR
Experience designing, implementing, and running a tiered NCR classification and disposition system at production rate, including Use-As-Is and Repair disposition authority
Direct experience chairing or co-chairing a spacecraft Qualification Review and making the independent go/no-go determination
Familiarity with PPL management, derating analysis, lot acceptance testing, and radiation qualification requirements (TID, SEE)
Demonstrated record of building multi-discipline assurance teams spanning all seven functions
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Systems, Electrical Engineering, or related field — or equivalent verifiable experience
Bonus Points for the Following
Direct experience with constellation programs and fleet-wide conformance reporting
Familiarity with SAP (Special Access Program) assurance requirements
Prior experience as CCB chair in a high-rate production environment
Familiarity with CMMI or AS9100 quality management systems in a space or defense manufacturing environment
Range safety certification or prior direct range safety interface experience
Additional Requirements
This is a fast-paced, high-impact environment - flexibility to occasionally work extended hours or weekends during critical periods is expected.
This is a full time, exempt position, based out of our Saratoga office.  The target base pay for this position is $190,000- $225,000annually.  The total compensation packaged will be determined by various factors such as your relevant job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.  
 
We are redefining how satellites are designed, manufactured and used—so we’re looking for candidates with passion, deep knowledge and direct experience on LEO satellite component development, design and in-orbit activities. If that’s your experience – then we’ll be immediately wow-ed.
 
This role requires access to controlled technical data. Under U.S. law (ITAR/EAR), we can only consider U.S. persons (U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and individuals granted asylum or refugee status). 
 
E-Space is not currently able to provide employment sponsorship for candidates who do not hold work authorization for the location of this role.


Why E-Space is right for you:

As a member of our team, you will play a crucial role in driving our success.  Our team members have a strong sense of dedication and responsibility; this includes a strong commitment to our mission to create an entirely new suite of global capabilities to improve lives, business efficiencies and build a smarter planet. This means that there will be times when extra hours, including nights and weekends, may be needed to meet critical deadlines and mission goals.  In return, we offer a dynamic work environment with opportunities for professional growth and development and the chance to make a meaningful impact in a high-growth industry.  

We want you to make the most of your journey at E-Space. That’s why we support and invest in the physical, emotional and financial well-being of our team members and their families. Some of what you can expect when working at E-Space:

•  An opportunity to really make a difference
•  Sustainability at our core
•  Fair and honest workplace
•  Innovative thinking is encouraged
•  Competitive salaries
•  Continuous learning and development
•  Health and wellness care options
•  Financial solutions for the future 
•  Optional legal services (US only)
•  Paid holidays
•  Paid time off

existing_roles.title: Head of Operations Planning and Special Projects
existing_roles.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Bedrock's technology is scaling rapidly —over the next twelve months, we will rapidly scale our machine count, partners, and sites while also adding net-new machine types and a next-generation platform.  

The Head of Operations Planning & Special Projects owns aligning cross-functionally on an integrated machine plan across types, generations, product lines, partners, sites in order to develop Operational headcount and material plans; ultimately, giving the business a clear view of what's required and by when. 

You'll own the integrated machine plan, scenario planning, cross-functional alignment when constraints arise, building headcount scaling factors and plans, and standing up our early Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Reporting to the VP of Operations, you'll be a critical thought partner to the VP and each Operations Lead.


WHAT YOU'LL DO


INTEGRATED PLANNING

 - Own the integrated operations plan covering requirements across all product lines, machines, field headcount, and material readiness.

 - Identify constraints in the plan and build scenarios that drive resolution or acceptable alternatives.

 - Partner with each Operations leader to surface optimizations, risks, and constraints, and develop paths to mitigation.

 - Support senior leadership and board-level decisions with clear, rigorous analysis.

 - Partner with the VP of Operations to define team OKRs, the mechanisms to track them, and routine reporting on critical initiatives.

 - Contribute to the long-term forecast, integrating priorities across multiple teams.

 - Help align data collection needs with operational optimizations to strengthen our data pipelines.


S&OP PROCESS IMPLEMENTATION

 - Partner with Commercial, Finance, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Operations to build stage-appropriate S&OP processes that tee up critical business decisions, surface constraints, and evaluate alternatives.

 - Own the monthly S&OP cycle end to end: forecast development, demand review inputs, forecast analysis, supply plan integration, pre-meeting coordination, and reporting.

 - Forecast demand, assess whether projected supply can meet it, and define key performance metrics such as forecast accuracy and fulfillment rate.

 - Serve as the bridge between business strategy, engineering build plans, finance, and supply chain execution.


PRODUCTION PLANNING COORDINATION

 - Own phase-in / phase-out planning for new machine types, product lines, partners and sites, and hardware generations — including availability, supply constraints, retrofits, and partner transitions.

 - Track lead times and drive alignment on critical decision timelines and order dates.

 - Work with Operations leaders to plan labor availability, using key ratios and operational planning drivers.

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Contract Manufacturing to plan production capacity against demand, consolidate risks, and drive prioritization when supply is constrained.


OPERATIONS INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS

 - Own the development of core operational metrics and routine reporting.

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to the business.

 - Support continuous improvement across Operations through process and data.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - A single, trusted integrated plan that the business uses to make decisions about machines, people, and materials.

 - Constraints surfaced early, with clear scenarios and recommendations — not surprises.

 - A functioning monthly S&OP cadence with consistent participation and clear decisions.

 - Core operational metrics defined, tracked, and reviewed on a regular rhythm.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - 8–10 years in operations, planning, or program leadership, including 5+ years working with cross-functional teams distributed across sites or regions.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence leaders — aligning cross-functional stakeholders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth.

 - Track record implementing S&OP or supply-and-demand processes that bring clarity to requirements, decisions, and success criteria.

 - Experience planning and managing hourly / field workforce headcount.

 - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; able to turn data into operational decisions.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including with executives.


PREFERRED

 - Familiarity with autonomy, heavy machinery, and/or the construction industry.

 - Experience standing up supply-and-demand review processes that clarify timelines, requirements, decisions, risks, and solutions.

 - Continuous improvement, Lean, or Six Sigma experience, including standing up an improvement program.


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

As Bedrock scales, the hardest problems are increasingly about coordination: getting the right machines, people, and parts to the right sites at the right time. This role builds the planning backbone that lets every Operations team — and the company — make faster, better decisions with confidence.

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

existing_roles.title: Head of Manufacturing
existing_roles.description:
Company Description:

Critical Energy is an innovative, early-stage, venture-backed cleantech company on a mission to accelerate the global energy transition through abundant, low-cost clean energy. Founded by an ex-SpaceX engineer, Critical Energy designs and manufactures factory-built, modular power plants. These rapidly deployable systems convert heat into electricity using a closed-loop thermodynamic cycle and can be installed in just weeks.

Critical Energy’s technology delivers high-efficiency, 24/7 power for geothermal applications and waste heat recovery (including from data center gas turbines), making clean energy practical and cost-effective for demanding sectors like AI hyperscalers and data centers. Backed by top climate and technology investors, Critical Energy is scaling rapidly.



Our Mission:

To build an abundant, low-cost, 100% clean energy future through groundbreaking geothermal innovation.

We are a team of passionate engineers, designers, and visionaries building cutting-edge solutions to meet the world’s energy needs with 100% clean energy. We are in the initial stages of development and building our team. This is your chance to join on the ground floor of something big! If you are ready to work at a fun, fast-paced, groundbreaking organization that is positioned to revolutionize geothermal energy, apply today!



About the Role:

We are seeking our first Head of Manufacturing to own the end-to-end build-out of our production capabilities from the ground up. You will design and stand up production lines for modular power systems, control inventory and costs, and build the manufacturing organization. This is a hands-on leadership role - you will be on the floor building, problem-solving, and leading by example while structuring processes for rapid ramp-up. You will collaborate closely with engineering and leadership to simplify designs for manufacturability, drive costs down toward the idiot index (minimizing cost relative to raw materials through smart process design), and deliver reliable modules on schedule and budget.



Responsibilities:

 - Lead the design, commissioning, and optimization of production lines for modular power units from scratch.

 - Build and scale a high-performing technician and manufacturing team in a startup environment.

 - Drive production ramp: pilot modules in 2026 followed by volume scaling in 2027 and beyond.

 - Own manufacturing strategy, process simplification, cost estimation/control for lines and products, and continuous improvement

 - Get hands-on with assembly processes

 - Implement production algorithms and workflows that prioritize simplicity, speed, and cost collapse.

 - Partner with engineering to influence design for manufacturability and scalability.

 - Build robust supply chain interfaces, quality systems, and safety protocols.

 - Ensure all product compliance documentation is available to ensure commissioning acceptance.

 - Foster a mission-driven culture aligned with climate impact and rapid innovation.



Required Qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing or mechanical engineering or another related field, or the equivalent experience

 - 5+ years of proven experience building and scaling production lines in complex modular or large-scale assembly environments such as aerospace, industrial processing, energy,, oil and gas, or automotive.

 - Strong background in fluid systems, mechanical assembly, metallurgy, and manufacturing processes such as welding, brazing, bolted joints, 5-axis machining, 3D printing, heat treatments, etc.

 - An established network of hardware suppliers and an understanding of what value they bring as compared to their competitors/contemporaries.

 - Startup mentality: comfortable getting hands dirty, wearing multiple hats, and thriving in ambiguity.

 - Deep understanding of production economics: able to estimate and drive down costs to create and operate manufacturing lines.

 - Track record of scaling technician workforces and transitioning from prototype/low volume to higher volume production.

 - Mission-oriented with genuine interest in climate tech, contributing positively to the planet, and energy transformation.



Bonus Experience:

 - You have been part of a team that designed and commissioned a power generation or processing plant

 - Experience designing for classified hazardous areas (NEC Class I Division 2) Experience with compliance to ASME B31.1

 - Experience with rotating equipment such as turbines, compressors, and pumps and their assembly



Compensation:
